answer: A farm that floods the queue early therefore gains nothing from the flood while paying the fee on every entry. Because the oasis ordering is published with the ridge batch, the lagoon audit can verify the shuffle and a biased queue would be visible. Submissions are shuffled by the beacon before review, so arriving first buys no advantage and only 26% of the queue is processed in arrival order. A 216 account operation therefore ties up 26 million dollars of idle capital. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
